text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

Initially I was a little disappointed with the Paperwhite because of my own lack of patience and constant comparing it to my other devices. I had to get use to swiping the screen to wake it up, understand the basic settings operations, and generally become comfortable with this model. I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

I am so glad that I did. My only complaint is that I wish Amazon would have included some kind of cheat sheet to get users started. It would have gone a long way to prevent my initial meltdown. If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

That is what this power adapter is for me, the alternative to connecting a Kindle to a computer. Just grab the adapter, connect your Kindles USB cable to it, plug the mini USB2 plug into your reader, and plug it into a nearby wall outlet. You'll be fully charged in no time.

The Kindle 5-watt USB power adapter is one of the best investments you can make.

UPDATE: December 2014... The charger is not properly charging the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 at high-speed. It still charges the Kindle Paperwhite at a reasonable speed. I don't know why the difference in performance unless there is some voltage drop or other internal issue. I have a charger from a Lenovo A10-70 tablet that can charge the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 at high-speed, though.

text_fidelity_a:
turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus I'm really impressed with this bluetooth receiver. Unlike another brand I tried, this offers outstanding sound quality, which is my main reason for using it.

It's very straightforward to set up. Just plug in the receiver (it's very small - less bulky than most "wall warts" that are present on power plugs), pair it with your bluetooth source, and plug the included cables into a stereo.

I'm using this with a Kindle Fire 8.9. Pairing was quick and simple.

The connection to the stereo can be done via a single cable or using a two cable (L/R) setup. Cables for both options are included. I'm using the L/R option, and plugged the cables into the TAPE input on my stereo receiver.

The sound quality is excellent. It is very hard to tell the difference in quality when streaming audio via this receiver versus playing a CD on the receiver. Movie dialog was outstanding as well.

The fact that it does not require a battery is a plus and a minus. On the plus side, no need to worry about recharging or swapping batteries. On the down side, it was a bit of a problem for me to get the cables routed since the wall outlet near my stereo is not easily accessible. I wound up running a short extension cord so that I could plug in the receiver close enough to the stereo so that the L/R cables would reach.

As a bonus, it includes a USB port so you can use it to recharge your phone/tablet/etc.

That one minor issue aside, I'm very impressed with the performance of this product. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: turelar Compatible Headphone Jack Dongle Adapter for Phone X 8/8plus 7/7plus

text_fidelity_a:
OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.
text_fidelity_b: OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage Bought this router a few days ago and have already begun the return process. I didn't have a good gut feeling about this router from the start, partly because the reviews are not all raves and partly simply because it looks kind of...evil to me. I am definitely not a fan of the hyper-aggressive router design trend that seems to be targeted at adolescent male gamers. I do not look at this thing and think it looks cool and feel positive feelings; I look at it and feel...apprehension. As a physical object, it's not something I really want in my apartment. But I decided to give it a try anyway because I don't think that kind of gut feeling should be one's primary consideration in choosing a router, and because I often like having the latest, cutting-edge tech and thought it would be nice to be ready for Wifi 6 for when I eventually get an iPhone 11 or some other device that features that protocol. But unfortunately, the negative experiences do not come only when I look at the thing.

I was at first alarmed, as I set up the router, by what a very long time it took anything to happen in the app. At every point at which I so much as switched to a different screen in the app, both during and after setup, the app would chug for an alarmingly long time before finally displaying the page I'd navigated to. This is to be expected when the router needs to restart, but...these were not points at which the router needed to restart. These were not points at which I'd changed any setting at all. These were points at which nothing at all had happened except that I'd attempted to go from, say, the app's main page to the Device Manager page, or the Wifi Settings page, or wherever. Simply switching pages in the app would take 20 or 30 seconds or longer. Another negative first impression.

I also noticed that the app doesn't give me access to a lot of the features of the router I expect to have access to. Granted, I'm an advanced user compared to a lot of people - networking is an aspect of computing I've enjoyed mucking around in for decades now, and my inclination with a new router (or an old one, for that matter) is to dive straight into areas of the settings where many ordinary users may fear to tread. But the Nighthawk phone app appears to be targeted more toward the average consumer. Which, if you're more the average consumer, is fine. But if you're me, you find that to be a disappointing restriction.

Then I started trying to use the web UI instead, and while it gave me access to all those more techy parameters I sought, I found the same delay problem happening when I tried to switch from one page of settings to another, but here it happened for longer, and sometimes the target page wouldn't load at all until I clicked again, this time on the blank page with the spinning progress indicator in the center.

So both of the means I have for interfacing with the router are inordinately slow, and one of them is clunky and glitchy on top of it.

And finally, add to all this the way I will occasionally go to navigate to any ordinary webpage and be told my browser can't display the page because I'M NOT CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET, and voila! - the straw that broke the proverbial camel's back.

This happens, and I go and look at the router to see if maybe it's restarted itself for some reason (automatic software update?) and...no. All lights are on and looking as they do during normal operation; the router's just not providing said normal operation.

I never once had such problems with the Apple AirPort Extreme I replaced with this router, nor with the Linksys AC5400 I bought more recently and then wound up giving to a friend. So, because I want a router that, unlike the AirPort Extreme, is tri-band, is still supported with software/firmware updates, and might also feature better performance with multiple connected devices, I bought myself another AC5400 with which I will be replacing this unsatisfactory Netgear thing as soon as it arrives.

And also because I decided I can wait for Wifi 6 until such time as I actually do have devices capable of taking advantage of it, which may be quite some time (i just bought a new MacBook Pro which doesn't support it, and I don't see the iPhone 11 as having any compelling advantages over my iPhone XS Max, soooo...).

The Linksys AC5400 is a monster among 802.11ac routers and has garnered much respect in tech mags and blogs and so forth. Plus I myself have about a year's experience with one and it's been fast, reliable, and glitch-free. So if you're looking for a new router and don't feel compelled to buy into 802.11ax just yet (few devices support it yet anyways), I heartily recommend that one.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Nighthawk 4-Stream AX4 Wi-fi 6 Router (RAX40) – AX3000 Wireless Speed (Up to 3 Gbps) | 1,500 Sq Ft Coverage

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) I recently purchased this to replace a lost remote for a piece of high end integrated amp. As with most things in the audiophile world, a replacement for this simple 6 button remote was way overpriced ($105) for what it is. So I was pleased to find that my amplifier was supported by the Logitech 650.

My biggest gripe is nearly a dealbreaker. After setting it up I went to use it on my integrated amplifier to raise the volume a little bit. The problem was that I couldn't just give the volume button a quick tap to turn up the volume a little bit. A quick tap of the volume raised the volume a significant amount whereas the original amp controller allowed me to make volume changes in small increments. After some searching I found that I just had to adjust the IR repeat length in the controller setup.

Problem solved, right? Wrong.

First issue was the manual being outdated. The frustration started when I tried following the steps in the manual. The first step was "Click Troubleshoot at the top of the Harmony Remote Software window". The problem was that there was no Troubleshoot button anymore. They had updated the software but didn't update the manual. Eventually I found the new location in the software where you can lower the repeats. The default was set to 1 so I lowered it to 0 (the lowest setting on the 0-4 scale). I saved my changes and after waiting for the remote to update I tried it again and it still was making large volume changes. With the remote already set to the lowest setting the only way I can make small adjustments to volume is to press the volume button and cover the IR emitter on the remote extremely fast so the volume change signal only gets sent out for a quick burst. I'm talking ninja fast. This is extremely annoying and tricky to get the hang of.

PROS
-Price
-Device Compatibility

CONS
-Can't make small volume changes
-Outdated Manual (they updated the software but didn't update the PDF manual with new instructions for the new software). This causes some serious frustration when you are instructed in Step 1 to press a Troubleshooting button that no longer exists.

Final thoughts... I bought this to mainly do one thing. Change volume and input selection on my integrated amp. The inability to change the volume in small increments is a constant annoyance. It should be something that can be fixed with a software or firmware update.

Logitech, please fix this on the software/firmware side.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green) I've been testing this speaker system with my 10" Samsung Galaxy Tab2 tablet which had no problems connecting to the speakers with and without the app from the Android store.

Appearance:
Their product description calls this 'fun, trendy and modern'. But to be honest this looks, to me, like an appliance that fell out of my grandmother's 1950's black, white and chrome art-deco kitchen. It's not unpleasant looking but I wouldn't call it modern. When I saw images of the system online I had hopes that the neon green ring around the face would light up. Sadly it doesn't. The handle is also fixed in place and doesn't retract or collapse into the body. It would have been a nice idea so you could stack or store this more easily.

Sound:
It doesn't sound bad. Especially for being just two 15 watt wide range speakers in a ported (holes to help the bass sound better) enclosure. The bass is a little flat and the high end sounds a little... hollow but it is a lot better than the speakers built into my tablet. I've tried a variety of music; jazz, pop, classical, rock, punk and everything sounded quite good. I found I had to use both the tablet's volume control as well as the speaker systems volume controls to get real volume out of the system. They operate independently of each other.

Drawbacks:
I don't normally comment on price with items received from the Vine program but at the time I'm writing this review Amazon is currently selling this item for over two hundred dollars. Maybe the Bluetooth equipment is expensive but to me that's a LOT for just two speakers in a box. I didn't pay that much for my four speaker bookshelf system or the subwoofer equipped speaker system connected to my desktop PC. Both of which have far superior sound quality.

The battery indicator light only seems to light up when the system is charging. I charged this a week ago and used it for several hours at a time but I have no idea how much charge is left in the battery.

The biggest problem I had with this speaker system was when doing anything other than playing music. I thought it would be fun to add big sound to the games I enjoy on my tablet but there's a distinct lag between doing anything and when the speaker plays the sound. I noticed it most of all in my favorite billiards simulator. You would strike a ball...and then hear it happen, even system sounds such as keyboard typing noises, a 'blip' when selecting things played a noticeable time after they happened.

The App:
I won't say much about the app here. It's completely unnecessary to operate this system with your Android device. It's just poor quality programming that appears to have been slapped together at the last minute. It also doesn't match the documentation and features such as Bass Boost which are in the instructions but don't exist in the app.

Speaking of the documentation. I opened the box and found a large booklet and for one, brief, moment I thought this item was fully documented in depth and detail... then I opened the instructions and found there's twelve pages of English instructions which are poorly written and lacking in detail. The rest of the book is comprised of numerous other languages each getting their own few pages. Ah well. Turn it on, turn it up. Enjoy the music.
text_fidelity_b: Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green)

text_fidelity_a:
3.7V 30W(peak) Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Double Subwoofer Rich Bass, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker Support FM Radio, Small Stereo Sound System for Home, Party, Outdoor Travel(No Light) I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing ten times (and more) what this does, the sound quality from this speaker is really quite good. In relation to the sound quality I would place them on par with mid to high end Bluetooth speakers.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in 4000 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 4.5 hours at max volume - 8 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF card, USB flash drive, or FM radio - it even has a built in extendable antenna.

While it has a remote and I tested it and it works fine, I rarely use it as I connect with my phone all the time.

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 4000 mAh, is much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been really good.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: 3.7V 30W(peak) Portable Bluetooth Speakers with Double Subwoofer Rich Bass, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Speaker Support FM Radio, Small Stereo Sound System for Home, Party, Outdoor Travel(No Light)

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) I've been using a Keurig machine for several years -- I currently own 2 of them. But I've always had an ethical issue with all the little plastic cups that get tossed into the environment. To that end, I've tried and used several different varieties of reusable K-cups, and had finally settled on the Ekobrew cups.

I was offered an opportunity to try this set, and decided to do a side-by-side comparison. The results were interesting. These Brewooze cups perform just as good as the more expensive Ekobrew cups.

I tried several different coffees and several different grinds. As with all reusable cups, you have to be careful how fine/coarse the grind is. Too coarse, and you get weaker coffee; too fine, and you get either overflow and/or sludge. I found that a medium-fine grind worked best for both cup brands. This way, I get the right strength and almost no powdery sludge in the bottom of the cup. One advantage of the Brewooze over the Ekobrew: I was able to use LESS coffee in the cup to get the right brew strength. With the Ekobrew, I needed to fill the cup; with the Brewooze, I filled it about 2/3 full to get the same flavor/strength.

As with all reusable K-cups, you need to take care when you seal them prior to use. These are no trouble to seal correctly -- you can easily see if there are gaps and do an extra "squeeze." Inserting them into the machine takes a bit of attention, too -- otherwise, you can pierce the cup. There are arrows on the lid that show which direction, so that shouldn't be a problem.

This set comes with 20 paper filters plus a replacement charcoal filter for the Keurig filter wand. I didn't see much advantage to the paper filters except possibly ease of cleaning. The coffee was weaker, and using a finer grind didn't seem to help. And it still resulted in some grinds getting "around" the paper filter and onto the mesh, so I still had to clean the cup. It's not a big deal, really -- the cups are easy to rinse clean after use. So I won't be using the paper filters, but you may find them useful.

I'm a little surprised at how nicely these performed, given the price. You get 3 cups (brown, medium tan, and light tan color -- the photo makes them look orange, but they're more of a tan/brown), so if you want to assign a color to different family members, there you go. Since I usually brew 2 cups into a large mug, I just fill 2 of them with the same coffee and run them one after the other in the morning.

kI have to say I was impressed. I didn't expect these to perform as well as they did. Definitely comparable to the Ek​​​​obrew so far -- the only question I have is durability, and only time will tell. I've been using these for about 4 days, and after the initial side-by-side test (when I brewed about 12 cups total), I've been brewing 2-3 cups every morning, rotating them, cleaning after each use, and so far, no signs of any wear problems. If I notice a serious issue, I'll update this review.

Sample supplied for review; opinions expressed are based on my personal experience with this product.
text_fidelity_b: Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black)

text_fidelity_a:
VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: VIMVIP USB Microphone, Microphone for Computer USB Mic for PC Desktop Laptop Condenser Microphone to Recording Podcast Gaming Streaming YouTube

I have no apple devices, but this worked immediately and perfectly for my Blackberry 9700, Xoom, and Win7 Laptop.

The first device pairs by itself, and devices 2-8 pair by holding 2 buttons for 5 seconds. After that, if multiple devices are turned on when you turn the headphones on, it seems to want to pick the first one you paired it with.

The BB picks it up as a Logitech Wireless Headset (not something generic), and you can then control the volume with the BB or with the headset itself (Did I mention the controls are all well positioned on the right headphone? - just two volume buttons, mic mute, micro USB charging port, and LED indicator), and you can also toggle between BB speaker phone and headset - they are obviously fully compatible - not generically. Pressing the mute button give you an audible cue, but does not change the BB display.

You'll never catch me in public with a normal bluetooth earpiece on anyway, so this is also great for calls at home - it will cancel out more background noise (because of the foam on both ears) so you can comfortably concentrate on your call. My tests show it working well more than the claimed 10m away (of course that partly depends on the other device's radio as well).

As another reviewer said, these sound good (and are capable of getting louder than I'll ever need), but are probably not as great as the full over-the-ear headsets. BUT, the wireless capability is really great to keep you fully uninhibited when exercising, cooking, or whatever you're doing when talking on the phone or listening to your music. For the record, I am 100% opposed to wireless shelf/tower speakers in a real home system, but this is a great solution for a headset.

Also, the mic backing out of the way is a must, so thankfully that is included. It not only pivots, but flexes toward or away from the mouth as well - very good design. Finally, the folding feature is great; any space saved is important. And the connecting wire connecting the two sides is accessible, if all that bending ever has it in need of a replacement.

Past helmet use has me thinking my skull is about as large as they come, and these are comfortable on me with the sides fully extended.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch

Wsky 60-100 Miles Transparent Digital HDTV Antenna - Best HDTV Antenna Indoor - Upgraded Silver Paddle Extremely High Reception - Support 1080P 4K Super Fun and Free for Life! My title for this review is not deliberately obtuse, it is just that I was desperate for an antenna and chose the one with the reviews that seemed to best meet my housing needs (apartment) as well as my budgetary needs (retired with small, fixed income).

You know, these small antenna types can only provide as well as they can, given their limited powers and whatever physical/geographic challenges are caused by one's limits on where the thing can be placed.

I do not live surrounded by mountains or trees or large buildings. I do not live in a valley or in the middle of nowhere. I DO live within forty miles of every transmission source in a nearby big city, so it might be considered reasonable to expect that an antenna that touts a sixty-mile range to be useful.

It is, but only partially because the fault is not in our stars, it is in a huge menu of influences (which may include the some sky/heavenly/ astronomical stuff, but that is another story).

My point, and the useful part, is that these simple and, more importantly, cheap antennas can only do what they can because geography, distance, obstacles you cannot see or image and even the stars (yep) conspire to modify their successful use, and even all that can be affected by other stuff we are unable to anticipate or influence.

If you want an antenna that has a potential for reasonable performance, simply spend the considerable dollars that will buy a reasonably and consistent performance.

Sellers, provide honest claims so that purchasers will know what they are getting. Customers, be discerning so that you can use your dollars to get the best you and your critical thinking can provide.

As for me, hope springs eternal that I will someday be able afford an antenna that allows me to watch our local PBS stations and in the meantime I will ignore the religious (not aligned with my personal spiritual practices) and selling-stuff channels.

It is the best I can afford, and a little late-night cartoons never hurt anyone.

The four-star rating is only because I finally hold a decent perspective on all this jazz.
text_fidelity_b: Wsky 60-100 Miles Transparent Digital HDTV Antenna - Best HDTV Antenna Indoor - Upgraded Silver Paddle Extremely High Reception - Support 1080P 4K Super Fun and Free for Life!

text_fidelity_a:
IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women At time of writing, this is going for $30, but I think it may have been $20 previously. I was surprised to see those prices, because it seems pretty sophisticated. I don't have an Apple watch, but I don't imagine it does much more than this (although I could definitely be wrong). It's a shame that wearing a watch sort of irritates me because I can see a real point to having this, surprisingly.

I think the Apple watch may have wireless charging, whereas this uses a magnetic cable with a USB port on one end. This can be just a little tricky to ensure it's charging while on its side (I guess face down is fine, but then you can't be 100% certain it's actually charging), but you get the hang of it quickly.

You get a surprising amount of information on the small face, and then a few scrolls in whichever direction can give you more information. You get use to that very quickly, too, and it is, in fact, very intuitive. You can always find what you want before too long.

The main face can be flash updated, meaning you can download different themes to the device. There's a couple neat ones, but nothing too exciting. I'm guessing there may be user uploaded versions for the Apple version (or maybe not, as Apple always locks its stuff down too much), and that could happen here, too, but I'm guessing not as many people have this, which will lessen the available "content".

The step count is the main thing, along with the time. The watch usually pops on for you to see it when you raise it to look at it, but not always. Usually a shake will turn it on if it doesn't notice you raise your arm. If nothing else, you can press the button. It's a fine line, because too many false positives would also be annoying.

It seems to last a very long time, like many days. And the battery indicator has five segments instead of the three that some devices have, so you get a better indication of when you'll have to charge it.

I'm not really convinced it's super accurate with my steps, but I'm not sure the Apple version would be either. And then it makes a guess on your calorie burn based on steps, which is just for fun as far as I'm concerned. It can do a bunch of other stuff if you hook it up with your "health" app, but I never bothered setting up that app in the first place.

Other convenience factors include it vibrating when you get a call or text, which can help you notice calls and texts, especially if you have your phone on vibrate all the time like I do (and for that reason miss a lot of calls). You can also read your text messages on here, although not really so well that you wouldn't just pull your phone out of your pocket if you actually want to read it (although knowing if you can ignore it can be helpful). You can also control your music to some degree and tell your camera to take a picture, which will be wonderful if you're one of those people always taking pictures of themselves (of if you just want a picture of you and your friends without having to have someone stay behind to press the button).

It also has a timer. Some of these things require the app to be running on your phone (I'm not saying which ones for sure because I think the manual said the camera shutter wouldn't work without the app, but it does). And there is a "find phone" feature which I can't figure out how to get to work, although I haven't tried much. I mean, it's bluetooth, so if the phone is far away, it won't help you anyway.

The watch and the band look just like the Apple version from what I can tell. The band also comes off easily, so I'm assuming it can be replaced with anything that fits the Apple version, but double-check before you count on it.

Overall, I like it a lot. I'd never consider the Apple version, which I assume costs hundreds, but for a fraction of that, I think it's a pretty cool toy.
text_fidelity_b: IDEALROYAL Smart Watch, Fitness Tracker for Android Phones, Smartwatch with Heart Rate,Sleep Monitor,Activity Tracker with IP67 Waterproof Pedometer Watch for Android & iOS for Men Women

text_fidelity_a:
Magellan Triton 400 Waterproof Hiking GPS I have a Garmin e-trex GPS as a backup for my sailboat navigation system so my use of handheld systems has been limited to marine use only. At first I thought this Magellan Trinton 400 system would be a good handheld for marine use. Then I changed my mind.

1. Yes, this 400 is in color... but the battery life is half that of my e-trex and I would much prefer longer battery life than a color screen. This is personal bias of course and may not be of importance to you.

2. I noted the 400 was much larger than my old e-trex and seemed "clunkier".

3. However, the biggest frustration was attemping to link the 400 with my boat's navigation program on my laptop. I simply wasn't able to link and their website help page was close to worthless. Never was able to link. My e-trex links right away.

4. I should have been able to download marine charts to the 400 but after several hours on their website, I was also unable to do this.

5. Finally, it was discouraging to google "Triton 400" and find so many negative comments about the unit and Magellan's support.

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White) Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.
text_fidelity_b: MP3 Player with Bluetooth and WiFi, 4" Full Touch Screen MP4 MP3 Player with Spotify, Android Streaming Music Player with Pandora, Portable HiFi Sound Walkman Digital Audio Player with Speaker (White)

text_fidelity_a:
VIZIO SB3820-C6 38-Inch 2.0 Channel Sound Bar The sound from this bar is clean, clear, crisp and LOUD! A very decent amount of BASS, with a sub woofer output should you want to connect one. I found out I ordered a longer bar than is recommended. How did I find out? The packaging for this bar states that it is for a 42" or larger TV. I purchased it for a 32" TV. The concern, I believe, is that if the speakers are too far from the TV's center it will not seem as though the audio is coming from the actors. My brain is making the leap and tricking me so all is well. I use my TV for music for the most part anyway (Comcast Music Choice and Fire TV Music).
It is disappointing that Fire TV Music has such poor audio quality since it is there that I can make personal music choices unlike Comcast. Fire TV just sounds plain bad. It did on the TV speakers and now on the bar; it is just un-listenable. Safe to call it "LOW FIDELITY"
As far as connecting an input to this bar from your TV you have many options and most all the cables you may need are included. I really liked that they included the cord to to connect the bar to a sub. This cord is over and above what is required to connect the bar to the TV...very nice touch VIZIO. Now I need to go to my storage and try to find my sub :-)
My TV only offers 2 audio outputs, head phone and optical. Included with the bar were a headphone-to-2 RCA connector cord, and a fiber optic patch cord, among others. That allowed me what would be considered the worst quality connection and the best quality connection possibilities. If you don't have OPTICAL OUT on your TV do not despair...the worst possible option (headphone-to-RCA patch cord) sounds FANTASTIC! I can detect no loss of fidelity between the two. You will not be missing out.
Now to the reason I gave it 3 stars rather than 5. The back of the remote just keeps sliding off. It is not broken in any way. Just poorly designed. I often use the sound bar in dark or nearly dark conditions. It is taking time to train myself to not go where I normally would to use the any of the buttons. So how about the POWER button? It is not the top left button on the remote as you will see and are used to on any other remote in your home. For some strange reason instead of the power button being in the far upper left of the remote they felt this was a good place to position the INPUT button. Power is upper right. Volume UP/DOWN is traditionally placed on the left side of the remote with a paddle switch or separate buttons. Located in the standard volume UP/DOWN positions are the TruVolume and the TruSurround HD. The volume UP/DOWN are located on a FLAT 1-3/8" (34.9mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) multi-function EVER SO SLIGHTLY RAISED square. To be honest I can't even tell that it IS raised at all most of the time. If you go for the volume in low light you may operate any of 3 other function controls. Lastly, if you were hoping the VOLUME controls are the 2 well raised buttons on the right (traditional location) you would be wrong. Those are your BASS/TREBLE controls.
I am not sure I would buy this bar again knowing what I do now about the remote. As I said I often use the remote in low or no light. The problems I mention here may just be my own...but I doubt it. All of these tiny buttons and controls are all scrunched into a small 2-3/8" (60.3mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) upper 40% of this little remote and they are not raised enough and not far apart enough to be used just by touch. I well believe that just 3 functions on the remote will account for 90% of it's use. POWER (that CAN be felt but it is in the wrong place...you'll get used to that) and the VOLUME UP/DOWN that exist on a square, fully smooth (NO tactile feedback...I'd hate to see a blind person trying to operate), 4-function piece of plastic that is raised about 1/32" (0.8mm). On the bright side for me, I found out fairly quickly that my cable box remote controls the basic functions of the sound bar. I hope you get so lucky.
Knowing what I know now I should have purchased a bar in the 28"-32" (71mm-81mm) class looking for features such as the control panel on the bar being mildly illuminated and a proper remote perhaps with illumination itself. My roommate may buy mine from me for a location that is always well lit and has a 42" TV. I'll lose $20 on the deal but I can get the absolute right bar for me.. I don't return items that are not what I would like due to my own failure in researching. So, for better or worse, the bar is mine. There is one thing you cannot fault; THIS THING SOUNDS AMAZING!
- Good Shopping!!!
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO SB3820-C6 38-Inch 2.0 Channel Sound Bar

This little guy is strong and bright! I've tried several lights, including handheld (like this), panel lights, ring lights, etc., and I have been very impressed with this one.

Before I dive into the good, let me discuss the bad: the iPhone app. I'm all for having an app to control the light and I totally understand why it's necessary. HOWEVER, this app REQUIRES that you sign up with an email and password. While there might be benefits to this (like accessing presets/settings across devices); I didn't check. Registering an account should 100% be optional. There is no reason to require me to register with my email + password so I can control this light via Bluetooth. As an aside, according to the Apple App Store, the developer does not collect any data from your phone (see pic); this is the reason I did not deduct a star for this.

My second gripe with the app, is that the it is a little rudimentary. Not particularly polished; and a little buggy at times (e.g. I couldn't get effects to kick in after selecting them on the app (I'd have to do it multiple times before the light would react), the light wouldn't always connect on the first try, etc. This was not the norm, but it happened a few times during my testing.

Now onto the good: First and foremost, it is BRIGHT. Brighter than similarly-sized lights. Physically, it feels well-designed. It has a 2000 mAh battery (I expected 1000 mAh). It is intuitive to operate and you can use it without the app if necessary (setting color temp, intensity, etc. No effects). There is a USB-C port for charging and a small display on the top, which shows battery %, time remaining (!), and color settings.

The soft cover on the front is attached magnetically, and can be attached to the back when you take it off (!); a wonderful design touch that is much appreciated. The light can also be affixed to metal surfaces via the magnet in the back.

The app, while barebones, provides a lot of functionality. There are many effects to choose from, and even a "music" mode in which the light will pulse to the beat of music picked up by your iPhone (or whatever device you are running the app on).

Overall, I have been really pleased with this light.
text_fidelity_b: IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow

TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200) This review is for the TP-link AC750 Dual Band WiFi Range Extender

I am using this on a network that has a Mac Mini, a couple of iPhones and an iPad. None of these devices could print to both printers; it was one or the other and not both on every single Apple product. After trying everything I could think of, I bought this extender and tried to set it up using the Quick Setup instructions. Anyone EVER had the experience of those Quick Setups working? I haven't and I've been using this stuff for decades. After Quick Setup failed to do anything other than connect to my router and open my network up to anyone that could get signal, I tried a different approach.

The EASIEST WAY TO SET THIS UP is to use the WPS button on your router and on the device. Press the WPS button on the router, then, press the WPS button on the extender. After a minute or so, the router and extender are paired/connected and the result is a secure connection to the router (uses the router's password--you do have a password don't you) with a much stronger signal in what were dead zones. Placement of the extender is sort of an experiment and moving it from plug to plug will show you the best location. Moving the extender after pairing does NOT foul up the connection.

I have two printers, a Samsung M2070W laser and an Epson Eco Tank inkjet. Both have wireless capability and can use WPS setup. To setup other WPS capable devices, just press the WPS button on the ROUTER and then the WPS button on the next device you want to connect. The connection to the router goes through the connected extender with no problem and does not interfere with the router/extender pairing. Do each device one at a time.

This was the solution I needed and now all wireless devices work together. It's a neat solution to solving signal strength and connectivity that can be an enormous hassle when using multiple devices from different makers.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wifi Range Extender | Up to 750Mbps | Dual Band WiFi Extender, Repeater, Wifi Signal Booster, Access Point| Easy Set-Up | Extends Wifi to Smart Home & Alexa Devices (RE200)

Wacom Intuos Small Bluetooth Graphics Drawing Tablet, 4 Customizable ExpressKeys, Portable for Teachers, Students and Creators, Compatible with Chromebook Mac OS Android and Windows - Black I love this little tablet. It's an inexpensive way to sketch: Particularly if you get the pistachio, which was $20 less then the boring black one when I bought it. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

I particularly like that it works with Android (at least on phones that support USB OTG, which is most these days). It would have been even better if the Bluetooth worked with Android, but at least with my Pixel 4, it didn't.

It doesn't come with any Android software, but Autodesk Sketchbook is free, and it's quite full of features. Sketchbook also runs on Windows 10.

The pen does not have an eraser like my *really* old Wacom bamboo did (you flipped the pen upside down, and it keyed the erase function). But I got used to it pretty quickly. (On the desktop, you can program one of the buttons on the tablet to switch to eraser). The model with an eraser is a lot more expensive, and I don't know if the eraser would work with Sketchbook in any case.

Corel Painter Essentials seems nice: I haven't used it a lot, because I've usually been on my phone. The first several times, it nagged me to upgrade, but it's stopped doing so. The "AI photo painting" bit is fun, but it's pretty slow, even on a pretty beefy i7. I was hoping that the software had an API, so then I could just auto-generate all of the various options, but it doesn't appear to.

Anyway, it's a ton of fun, and it's got me drawing stuff again.
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Intuos Small Bluetooth Graphics Drawing Tablet, 4 Customizable ExpressKeys, Portable for Teachers, Students and Creators, Compatible with Chromebook Mac OS Android and Windows - Black

BT-C2400 Battery Charger Analyzer Tester for AA AAA NiMH NiCd Rechargeable Batteries I'm very pleased with this AA/AAA battery charger. I have another Opus that I use for Li-ion charging and have been very satisfied with the performance over the years. This has all the same features (selectable charge rate, discharge/charge cycling, lots of info on the display) but rather than have the sliding posts to hold the batteries, this has fixed posts position to hold either an AA or an AAA. It's a more reliable and secure way to hold the batteries, especially the AAA size, compared with the sliding posts.

Although this has loads of features for those who like to dive into those areas, it can also be used in "simple" mode -- just insert the battery. It defaults to charge mode at 400 mA, which is perfect for AA and AAA cells. Zero button pushing needed -- just pop in the batteries and you're done.

I have a variety of charger brands in use, but Opus and Gyrfalcon have never let me down in terms of performance, build quality and longevity. Highly recommend!

The matt brushed finish does look pretty fancy but I don't know why they leaved some part unbrushed. So some part looks pretty nice but some look like just plastic. Sound Quality : I am not so sure about this part. This does have all the functions which earbuds should have (touch control, voice calling etc) but it simply lacks the depth of the sound. It sounds like slightly improved version of Air plane bundle earphone, so not worth to discuss about base/mid/high range. For sound quality, something is off in the sound quality.

Ergonomics: So this one has old Air Pods design, you cannot change the soft rubber to adjust the size to fit your years. After few hours of use, I felt uncomfortableness and slight pain with this ear phone but I have small ear and I feel pain with Air Pods as well, so my opinion is not so important for this matter I guess.

Buy if you are looking for : some quick substitute for your Galaxy Buds / Air Pods / or other ear buds and price is very important for your purchase decision. Interestingly, this earbuds mic is weirdly good.

Don't if you are looking for : earbuds with excellent sound quality / very comfortable fit

It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

The bottom line: I was skeptical. I've owned Samsung plasma and LED and an LG LED recently and I see no material difference between the TCL and the other LEDs. All the positive reviews here, plus the CNet reviews/primers on Roku integrated TVs put me over the edge. We really like this TV and it's simplified our streaming incredibly. Go get it!

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I knew right away that these would be my office headphones. I have a mechanical keyboard that I use at work, and the office I work in is semi-open. There's a *lot* of noise coming every-which-way. These are a much-needed accessory to my work productivity, as I'm easily distracted by things in my periphery, whether visually or auditory.

The presentation is great. The box is very high quality, reminiscent of the recent Samsung Galaxy device boxes. A smooth matte feel with gloss--weirdly pristine. The box slides out of the slipcover and you get the headphones already in the case. What I like is that they're folded, and there's even a little sheet underneath the phones that always reminds you how to put them back in. Also included is a 3.5mm cable in case you don't want to use Bluetooth, a charging cable, and an adapter. The case is nice, but as I keep mine at work I can't testify to its durability. There's a thin mesh net on the backside in case anyone needs to store one or two thin headphone accessory/-ies along. The accent colors are a nice light copper/rose gold color. I love that color; I'm glad it's getting more attention in recent years.

It didn't take long to charge the headphones, so they come with a little bit of juice. As soon as you turn them on, you get a soft beep along with a voice indicating they're turned on. Nice responsive feedback. Once I put them on I could hear the headphones working to drown out the sound; there was a thick veil of soundproofing that was draped over my ears as soon as the earpads touched them.

The first thing I did was listen to podcasts through the Pocket Casts app and .flac music through Poweramp v3. With podcasts, the difference was phenomenal. Listening to "Wait, wait... Don't tell me!" made me feel as though I were in the audience. The music was fantastic...until I tried on my other headphones which I use for music only.
I thought the bass might've been too strong with the Sony headphones, and I was right. After using even "cheaper" headphones like the Audio-Technica M50x, I could tell the Sony had too much bass. I'm not sure if that's partly because of the noise-canceling technology or what, but the bass can be toned down a bit, methinks.

I then proceeded to download the supplementary app to get the fullest suite of attributes the headphones can get. The app works well, and I didn't experience any hiccups while actually using the app. The only hiccup was when I was trying to download the update. It took *forever*. Almost an hour and it was just halfway through. I decided to bring them to work the next day and let the app sit there while updating. Thankfully, it remembers the progress, even though the app kept crashing during the update process.

There are some optimization tweaks in the app, some sound profiles to let you configure the noise cancelation level (yes, level; the noise cancelation is pure software; you can set it to drown out the most noise as possible or have no noise cancellation at all), and even a little snippet of what is currently playing through the headphones. A simple UI with all the features you need.

The first few days I used it I was active, and I kept noticing that my ears sometimes would pop depending on whether I sat down or arose quickly. Another weird thing is that when I take the headphones off, my ears sometimes need a minute or two to adjust. There's so much noise in the world! After taking the headphones off I can hear HVAC activity and my loud work neighbor who's otherwise not that loud.

I had some headphones with some touch controls before and always found them tacky. I used them once when I first got them and never again. But with these headphones, I'm always using the tap gesture to play/pause and the swipe gesture to raise or lower the volume. There are also swipe gestures to skip or go back a track, but since I never do that anyway I never use those gestures. You have to be careful with the tap; when it works, it works. But the whole surface isn't the active portion and you have to hit it right in the center. Sometimes I'm hitting my finger against my ears trying to find the spot and hurting myself in the process. I tested the gesture where you put your entire palm on the cup to turn off the noise canceling feature and let the mic allow incoming conversation, but not after the third try. I could hear the other people just fine, but I found the right hand over my ear felt awkward, and one person didn't realize I could even hear them. Putting your hand over your headphones isn't a gesture people immediately see as you paying attention to them.

The headphones are extremely lightweight and comfortable to use; I left them on for about two hours once before having to take them off. I actually was surprised with how light they were; when I got the Amazon box I didn't believe it was my headphones. It was much lighter than expected.

For my first noise-canceling headphones I'm pleased. The sound balance can be better (less bass), but they make for fantastic headphones to use at work. I wasn't sure what I was expecting with noise-canceling technology. I thought it would drown out all noises, but you still can hear the occasional mutter; it just won't be distinct.

Oh, forgot to mention the battery life. I charged it only once and have been using it for a week, at about an hour or two each day. Still going well. If you press the power button once it will tell you the battery level. AFter the initial update the voice indicator might give the wrong battery level (it did for me), but give it about ten or fifteen minutes to adjust and it will go back to normal.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version)

text_fidelity_a:
Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home I’ve spent the last month using and playing games on the Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3. It’s a decent entry-level laptop. I wouldn’t consider it a dedicated gaming machine, but more aimed at daily use plus some gaming.

The laptop includes 3 free months of Xbox Game Pass, so I’ve played games available through that library. Games like Moonlighter, Moonglow Bay, Tunic, Sims 4, and Hades. The laptop handled all of those just fine, but many are older games and/or not very hardware intensive.

However, I don’t think 8GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD are enough. In my very first day of downloading games, I filled more than half the hard drive (and only ~236GB is available to start). As for the RAM, my 5-year-old laptop has 8GB of RAM and I’m feeling it. A laptop from 2022 should start with at least 16GB.

The Quad Vent fans vent in the back and on both sides of the laptop. I wish there wasn’t a vent on the right, because it’s right where the mouse sits. After maybe twenty to thirty minutes, my hand gets sweaty, which isn’t great when playing a competitive game.

There are 2 USB-A ports, one on each side. The back has an HDMI port, Ethernet, USB-C, and the power input. I actually really like the power input being on the back, as that way the cable isn’t in the way when using the mouse. But I’d like another USB-A port in the back, because I can see using a hub with this laptop.

The keyboard is not my favorite. On the plus side, it’s a full keyboard. I can’t remember the last time I saw a laptop with a numpad. The keyboard has backlighting, but only one color option: white. The keys are flat on top and somewhat slippery. The keyboard itself feels cramped, especially when gaming with WASD.

The laptop is heavy, about 7 or 8 pounds. It’s not something you’ll want to tote from class to class. The battery lasts about an hour if playing games, and about 3 hours for normal use.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaPad Gaming 3 - (2022) - Essential Gaming Laptop Computer - 15.6" FHD - 120Hz - AMD Ryzen 5 6600H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 - 8GB DDR5 RAM - 256GB NVMe Storage - Windows 11 Home

BSIMB Digital Picture Frame IPS Display, Wall-Mountable Electric Photo Frame with Remote Control, Place in Landscape&Portrait, Gift for Grandparents Frame is a tad slow to respond to the remote; that could be better. It isnt always slow, just sometimes it doesnt pic up, other times it is fast & perfectly fine. I think it has to do with distance from frame. Dont be too close!

They have a large frame with touchscreen available, so I would personally go with that unless price dictates otherwise. I like the remote too, just wish it responded faster and more consistently. I wouldn't want just a touchscreen. Option for either/both in one would be cool. Anyway.. I like this. It is my first frame. I have been kind of using our Echo Show, and sometimes just a computer screen. But I have wanted a basic frame, so here I am.

Basically plug it in, get it on the network, get the app, make an account, pair with phone, then select pics off phone to be loaded. Can choose up to 50 at a time. Very easy. Surprisingly so. I am tech savvy but impatient. This was pretty easy to figure out. Takes a few minutes to get them loaded.

Picture quality is quite good, and occasionally looks off. Thought that might be original source rather than the frame. All considered, all pics are quite clear and detailed.

if you have it set to full screen, then some pics may be cut off. If you have it set to the other option (cant remember the term), then the pics come up as you took them. Glad I figured this out because at first I had some that were cut off and it made me sad. Got it fixed very easily and all is well. YAY

Can set up calendar, weather, location, an alarm, play music, load videos. Can set time and make it a clock, can choose clock face. Can choose 12 hr or 24 hr format. Can create slide shows, decide on length of time, random or sequential or based on when taken. Very cool. Oh, and even incorporate music. Can label/add words/text too. Easy on, easy off.

Can operate basic stuff directly from the frame. Including very quickly rotating a pic. No need to use remote for everything!

Has headphone jack on back

It really isnt bad as an entry level frame. Would be nice as a gift if preloaded for someone. Now that I have been using this, I know what to look for in an upgrade. But this will certainly make do as i get to know it more and more. Ive only been playing with it for a day or so. The more I write about it, the more I like it.

I think pics can be emailed to this like Skylight subscription frame. Can let other people add photos.

Can also add photos/music/video via a SD/MC/SDHC, USB, USB mini, or thumb drive.

Needs to be plugged into wall receptacle.

Says in one of the product pictures that it can be wall mounted . I dont see how. It is a landscape mode item with a back portion to help it sit upright. It would not ever be flush with wall. I wouldnt buy it for that anyway. I got it for use on a side table so I can see pics of my dogs and cats all day long.

Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack I walk to school everyday, it's about a 30minute walk. That combined with all the time walking to different buildings once I'm at school, is a lot of time to get cozy with this backpack.

A little back story, I previously owned a unisex North face backpack, I got rid of it because it was too big and hurt my back. I downsized to a women's North face. It was better but it still didn't seem very comfortable and never felt very light even with few items in it.

Cut to this backpack, it's a women's backpack so it's made smaller. (Also I'm 5'7" 120lbs so I'm not terribly small bit still). This backpack feels lighter than others, I think it has to do with the frame, it's very comfortable on. I typically have 2 binders and two medium sized textbooks in my backpack, occasionally I'll bring my laptop. With everything in it, It doesn't irritate my lower back or shoulders after hours of wear.

The backpack also comes with 2 straps on the side that allows you to compress it in even further. When your stuff is closer to your back, and not hanging far out, it's a lot more comfortable. There are several pockets, a large padded pocket for your laptop, another for your books and such and 2 smaller but still very spacious pockets, as well as an interior pocket and nonzippered outer pocket.

The pockets do zip all the way around, but the straps will need to be unbuckled to do this. I'm not gonna lie, I'm very lazy and have not unbuckled the straps since getting this item, (it's been a month), and I've been able to get my books/laptop in and out without a problem.

The pockets for waterbottles are nice and deep so your water bottle won't fall out, and there's also a strap on either side to secure it even further.

The chest strap on this is awesome too. It doesn't compress your chest in an awkward or uncomfortable way which is something I always look for.

The shoulder straps and back are vented so it's been really great for me, a very sweaty person walking in the summer time. Haha

Overall I think this backpack is awesome! I've already recommended it to my school friends, looks like Osprey is my new go to backpack brand!:D
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Nova Women's Laptop Backpack
