text_fidelity_a:
Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment Note: There is more than one product attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the 18” light.

One of the things I have been researching for a while is ring lights. I have wanted one for a little while, but not the kind that sits on a desk and is only useful for making personal videos for upload. I wanted one that would be suitable for taking portrait photos and would be suitable for professional use. This is a nice ring light to that end and so far I am pleased with it, though I have not been using it long.

This is a large light, 18” in diameter which makes it quite a bit larger than most ring lights available right now. It is large enough that you can shoot photos or video through it using a full-sized camera with little effort, which is what I was looking for. It comes with a full-sized tripod (which it needs) as well as a nylon carry bag. It also comes with a mounting makeup mirror in the bag which is something I will not use with the ring light (I have other uses for it). In includes all of the hardware you need for mounting your camera, video camera or phone if you are a vlogger or content maker.

The very first thing I did with this light was point my camera right at it while using the electronic shutter, in order to determine if the LEDs in this light are strobing or not. I half expected these to strobe based on the price, but they do not which is a very good thing. It means steady, consistent light that does not flicker.

There are two adjustment knobs that are on the light assembly, one to control the brightness and the other to control the light temperature. The temperature range (speaking in generalized, observable terms rather than technical terms with numbers) allows for setting the light from an orangy golden-hour glow to a piercing frosty blue, and everywhere in between. So, though it may require some messing it allows for getting the light temperature just right based on skin tone and background. The brightness can be varied from a soft glow to bright enough to hurt your eyes when looking right at the ring. Thought not designed for such, this would work as a studio light in a pinch...

I do not have a light meter to check the actual light temperature or the lumens/lux output.

There’s a plastic cover over the LED array that helps to diffuse the lights and make them easier to face when using the light to illuminate a face for portraits.

The power source is AC 110/120. Some ring lights I have seen and used have USB-based power input instead. These tend to be smaller and less powerful.

Construction is good though I would stop short of saying it is solid and rugged. It is mostly plastic so it does have some flex to it but seems sturdy enough to handle getting moved around and jostled some. Because the housing is plastic instead of metal this is a lightweight unit and is easy to transport. This is a trade-off I have seen with tripods as well – lightweight for travel, heavier for less mobile work. This light seems geared for the traveler based on that.

Overall, I am pleased with this light. It is a bit better than I expected and it has everything you need in the package to be suitable for vlogging or studio use. It’s a big light so it does cost a bit more than a lot of the smaller, USB-powered lights out there but the cost is reasonable. If you’re looking for a ring light that can be used for either video content or of portrait work, give this one some consideration.
text_fidelity_b: Led Ring Light 18 Inch Selfie Light Circle Light kit with Tripod Stand, Dimmable 3000K- 6500K Lights for iPhone with Phone Holder, Lighting for Video Recording, Makeup, Live Stream, YouTube Equipment

text_fidelity_a:
Driveway Alarm Wireless Outside, 1byone Motion Sensor Alarm 1000 FT Range Extra Loud Chimes Home Security Alarm System with 1 Receiver 2 Weatherproof Infrared Sensors Protect Indoor/Outdoor Property Today I removed the unit from my front steps where it has been since I first received it almost 2 years ago. It had been causing the indoor alarm unit to sound without ceasing. I removed the batteries to see what might be the problem, and I found ANTS had taken up residency inside the sensor unit. After clearing as many ants as possible, I put the unit in a plastic bag that is sealed. It will be several days before I open the unit to clean the circuit board as well as the housing. Then I will attempt to seal all openings so that I can use the sensor. It may not operate reliably once all the openings are sealed, but I have no other choice.

The second sensor is not giving me any problem because it is in a location that ants will not frequent.

As for locating the sensor in my mailbox so I will know when someone has opened the mailbox door, that won't work. The metal mailbox prevents a signal from being transmitted the 100 feet to the alarm. Also, ants like to use the mailbox which makes me spray an insecticide when I see them, and that's usually once a year.
text_fidelity_b: Driveway Alarm Wireless Outside, 1byone Motion Sensor Alarm 1000 FT Range Extra Loud Chimes Home Security Alarm System with 1 Receiver 2 Weatherproof Infrared Sensors Protect Indoor/Outdoor Property

text_fidelity_a: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White Easy to setup and works like a charm @ first. Until it didn't. O.k. I must say I know enough about mesh networks to be dangerous but I must say something from the very beginning with the mesh system was strange. Alright it all started back at the beginning of the year where at certain times of night my internet would drag. I said, "NIGHT." Typically in the morning when everyone else is sleep. I am up working. I would notice download speeds of maybe about 25 and uploads at 10. So after a few days of this,  I contacted Xfinity internet support and ask them to run a check on the internet. Right away, the support guy said, "Log into your account and let me show you something."  I said O.k. and right there I am seeing the traffic go thru the roof. The rep said, "Oh yes there is a lot of traffic on for some reason coming from Somalia. I said are you sure. He said Oh yes.  Since I run a business I have backup internet thru another company that I can jump on in case my internet goes down.  So I disconnected my internet and and change the wifi mesh name and password. Later that morning, I noticed that the ssid was still broadcasting my old ssid name so I connected too it and noticed that I still had internet.  REALLY!!!!! I could watch movies and everything. Very strange. So I contacted Google support and was told to reset the mesh back to the original factory systems. Now for the last 4 to 5 months I have to change my ssid every few months and reset everything back to factory settings to keep my internet from dragging. I haven't read anything else about this expect a few bloggers and you-tubers say that they suspect that the mesh network can be hacked.  I must say after a few months of tracking my internet usage online I must say I suspect the same. If you purchase this check your usage regularly.  I have owned this mesh system since 2017 and didn't notice any problems until recently. Trying a new mesh network. It think it is time.
text_fidelity_b: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White

Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Some people prefer their headphones outside of their ears, with comfortable ear cushions and other features, such as the [[ASIN:B00007056H Koss KTXPRO1 Titanium Portable Headphones with Volume Control]]. Others prefer wearing their headphones in the privacy of their own ears, with the added bonus of noise isolation.

There are good reasons for choosing either type depending on your personal preferences, such as comfort levels, where and when you're using them, what you're listening to, and whether or not you have to share with other people.

For general use at home, I use the regular "outie", especially for movies or music with inappropriate language that I'd rather not play in surround sound in the presence of young `uns. I also let my son use it when I'd rather not hear another note from the Jonas Brothers. However, in the wee hours of the morning when the only creature stirring is me, I prefer to use in-ear headphones, which shut out everything except the music.

At work, I hardly ever use headphones due to the telephone ringing off the hook, but at lunchtime I sometimes use the in-ear headphones for peace and quiet. I drive to work, so no headphones are needed for the daily commute.

This is a fairly expensive model, but it's worth every cent if you can safely use headphones that cut out most external noise.

Pros:

1. Really nice packaging, easy to open, simple instruction manual
2. Cool, sleek and compact black metal carrying case included, with a cleaning tool and cable clip as accessories.
3. It comes with three different sizes of rubber caps, and as Goldilocks might say, one is for ears that are big, one's for smaller ears, and one will no doubt be just right. Changing caps is simple too.
4. It also includes a pair of memory foam sleeves that fit so snugly in your ears that you may think they belong there.
5. The caps are washable, once you dry them properly before using them again.
6. The sound is marvelous, clear and true, and there's no need to raise the volume to sonic boom levels.
7. The headphones are clearly marked left and right, and are at an angle for easy insertion and a tight seal
8. Drastically cuts down on external noise

Cons:

1. Unless you're using it for an IPod or other portable device, the cord is too short.
2. May feel a bit weird for some people due to the superior noise isolation.
3. You may experience "ewwwwwwwwwww" moments when your friends grab them and try them on. These aren't for sharing.
4. Try saying "in-ear headphones" out loud six times

If you're looking for an excellent pair of (deep breath) in-ear headphones, I think you'll be pleased with this one.

Amanda Richards, July 2, 2008
text_fidelity_b: Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS Overall, this is a very nice golf GPS for the price. I was a little worried about it being too complicated to use, but the manual explains all the features in reasonably good detail. I found it helpful to keep the manual with me the first couple of times I used it on the course to refer to, but after a few outings I felt comfortable using it.

I had an initial problem with the battery life in that it quit on me after about an hour of use. After leaving it in the charging cradle overnight, the next time it maintained its charge for a full afternoon's use. I've used it (and recharged it) several times since then and have had no problems, so it seems the first time was just a momentary glitch (or perhaps I didn't seat the charging cable firmly enough).

I very much like that it does not require a subscription to use, nor does it need to be tethered to a PC for the initial setup. It has a pretty extensive database of courses (Izzo says on their website that they cover 90% of the courses in the US). You can use their website to look up a course to see if it is included in the database.

Sat acquisition times is quick - took only a few minutes to get a lock and find my course the first time I used it. Acquisition time was even faster on subsequent uses. It uses a SiRF Star III receiver.

The display is clear even in sunlight, but it is a bit small for me. I don't usually have my reading glasses with me when I'm outdoors, so seeing the distance numbers took quite a bit of squinting. Granted, if you don't have aging eyes you won't find that to be a problem, but it would have been nice to have a larger display.

I also didn't find it all that comfortable to wear. It is lightweight and not too thick, but the strap was not very comfortable. Plus the greenish/yellow accent color (found on the inside of the strap and the sides of the unit) didn't appeal to me much - rather garish looking to my eye.

The warranty is only 90 days, which I think is too short given the price -- a year would be more appropriate.

But those are minor quibbles. Overall, the functionality is great - quick to acquire sats, accurate distances and straightforward to use. Considering the price of other brands, such as Garmin, this is a great value. Definitely should be on the short list if you're shopping for a golf GPS.

[As an aside, it's a real bear to the product out of the clamshell packaging. I didn't' factor that into the rating, but set aside some time to wrestle it out of the plastic jail it comes in should you buy one.]
text_fidelity_b: Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS

I like classical music, and the sound is so relaxing and immersive, I forget that I’m wearing earbuds. (It helps that these are totally without wires, of course.)

The earbuds are far and away the most comfortable that I’ve ever worn. You get three sizes of in-ear tips (S, M, L). There is NO sound leakage to speak of. I didn’t test the call-answering features or other features beyond playing music. The earbuds paired, without incident, with my iPad Pro and with my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge. The charging case seems to need to be charged up to the green light for pairing to work.

Three stars because I haven’t used the earbuds consistently for a full month. As much as I love these, I’m afraid that the left earbud will fail before long (as other reviewers have reported).

text_fidelity_a:
Antennas Direct DB2 Multi Directional HDTV Antenna (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I recently purchase an Antenna's Direct Clearstream 4 to use in my attic to feed the TVs in the BR and LR. Works fantastic, so when I needed another antenna for a TV in the study that I could not hook up to the antenna in the attic, I again went with Antenna's Direct, but this time picked the DB2 since it was smaller (and cheaper).

Absolutely fantastic reception! The only station it does not pull in as well as the Clearstream 4 was one fringe station. As with the Clearstream 4 positioning is a breeze - I just propped it up in the corner!

Given how well it performs, I thought I'd see how it does in the attic in place of the much larger and more expensive Clearstream. It does nearly as well - all the major networks come in equally good, and the DB2 picks up all but one of the more distant stations. The one it misses is a channel I never watch anyway, so for me, the two are equal.

For me (located outside Wash DC) the antennas pull in 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 5, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 9.1, 9.2, 14.1, 20.1, and about a dozen PBS stations rock solid. Channels 66.1 to 66.4 are so-so on the DB2 and pretty good on the Clearstream 4.

The Clearstream 4 also pulls in several analog stations. I didn't try that with the DB2 so I don't know if it will work with analog. Come February, the point will be moot anyway, so I didn't bother to test it out for analog.

So, if you're debating between the Clearstream 4 and the DB2 (or DB4), give the DB2 a shot first - the little guy may do the trick, and you can save quite a bit of cash.

It does the job- that is, it holds the TV in place securely. I did find that installation wasn't so simple, since the outlet is on the wall right behind it (to keep wires hidden) and this thing really HUGS the wall. I was kind of annoyed that after installing everything, I then realized I didn't have enough clearance to plug it in or reach any of the ports, so I had to take it down and use the largest bolts and spacers they had to give some space between the wall and TV to allow room for the cables.
One thing I noticed is that with ALL the spacers and longest sized bolts, the bolts were just a bit too long to screw all the way in securely. I ended up having to supplement my own using 2 metal washers in the middle of the array of spacers. They could have avoided this by just including a couple more of their thin spacers to make up for the extra length for people like me, but at least I got it working. I like that the TV easily comes off using the pull tabs, and I'm thankful that my 48" TV is large enough to hide the pull strings. I saw examples of other users mounting smaller TVs which show the strings hanging out the bottom. I wouldn't like that, and would probably tie them up or something to hide it. Not at issue at larger size screens I guess, but at least I like that it is easy to remove if I need to get to something behind it. Putting it back up on the wall is a 2-person job, not a big deal at all, but too hard to balance and click them on by myself.
For the money, it's a cost effective way to get your screen on the wall. I sorta wish I had gone for a slightly more expensive articulating arm one like my old one, since it makes getting to the back super easy without removing the screen, but those are more expensive and stick out further from the wall too. text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black) There are more than enough helpful reviews, product specs and Q&A, so I am going to focus on this tablet for folks who are upgrading from another Android tablet, and especially another Samsung. I'll say up front that the biggest reason [for me, anyway] is the extra screen real estate and resolution.

I had a small surprise in that mine did not come with Amazon apps pre-installed like they did on my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch, White) 2013 Model]] that it replaced. Locating the App Store application so I could install all of the applications that I have purchased was a bit of a hassle, but I finally got that resolved. Like my older Samsung tablet this one is a little less than spectacular when it comes to streaming music to a speaker via bluetooth. I do not know why Samsung cannot get it right on tablets because I have never experienced any issues streaming on my Note II and Note 3 phones.

Another issue of which you need to be aware is this tablet is thin and flexible. I knew that in advance and purchased a [[ASIN:B00KCDBD2E Samsung Galaxy Note Pro 12.2-inch Case Cover]], which in my opinion is one of the better cases for this tablet. The hard shell part of the case into which you insert the tablet provides a rigid casing that allows zero flex. No matter which case you ultimately select I strongly recommend that you get one.

You may have issues with some apps if you opt to install an SD card to expand your storage, or if you are moving an SD card from another tablet to this one. The KitKat version of the operating system will not write to SD cards under certain conditions. There is a free fix called SD KitKat Fixer by JRummy Apps that you can get from the Play Store. I highly recommend it. As a side note, I had no issues with this SD card: [[ASIN:B00N2ROG9O PNY Turbo Performance 64GB High Speed MicroSDXC Class 10 UHS-1]]. It is an inexpensive way to max out your memory. I have heard that this tablet will work with 128GB cards, but I have not tested any so cannot say for sure.

If you are accustomed to Samsung's user interface you will feel right at home. For me, after the little challenges I mentioned above I was fully up and operational on this tablet in a few hours. A lot of that time was reinstalling purchased apps from Amazon and the Play Store, tweaking my settings so that they mirrored those on my Tab 10.1 (which are identical to my Note 3 phone), and this feels as comfortable as an old shoe. A much larger old shoe to be sure, and it's incredible how much extra screen space you get going from 10.1 to 12.2.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 (32GB, Black)

Dash Cam Front and Rear CHORTAU Dual Dash Cam 3 inch Dashboard Camera Full HD 170° Wide Angle Backup Camera with Night Vision WDR G-Sensor Parking Monitor Loop Recording Motion Detection This is a very well made dash cam. It doesn't come with a memory card (mini HDMI needed), but comes with a coupon where you can get a memory card if you write an Amazon review. There are numerous pieces in the kit:
- The camera itself, including night vision LEDs and viewing screen
- Suction cup holder for mounting to the interior of the windshield
- Power cable with cigarette lighter plug
- Cable to connect to the backup light to function as a backup camera (not quite sure how this works)
- Fairly comprehensive English-only instruction book

The instruction book says that it has an internal battery that's used only to write the video to the memory card. I'm not quite sure how this is supposed to work, but I think you need to have it powered while driving. And I don't see how to do that without the power cord dangling all over the place, or doing some awkward routing of the power cord to the vicinity of your 12v power jack. If the same company has a similar unit that can run for 4 hours or so on an internal battery, I would be likely to buy that version of the product.

Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor This little device does a lot.
While it is sort of a smart watch, it sort of isn't, too. But what it does, it does well.

The good:
- Excellent selection of watch faces, including cute, clever, big, pretty, etc. You can change your face every day to match your clothes if you want.
- If I understand correctly, you can use it with other services, like Spark People.
- measures pulse, steps, miles. Tracks exercise on demand.
- motivates in numerous ways. Reminders to stand up, encouragement to finish your goal steps for the hour, challenges, even "travel" challenges that are longer term.
- large userbase. You can network with more of your friends on Fitbit than on any other fitness watch.
- big face without losing attractiveness
- large variety of replacement bands available from third parties, some very pretty.
- Can be used with many other fitness applications.
- Detects sleep surprisingly accurately
- Lots of settings options
- A decent number of apps available
- Handles the shower well
- If you never have to take it off except to charge, it's harder to lose it.
- Charges very quickly
- The charger is an awesome design and easy to use
- You can always have your alarms with you so you never miss them.

The irritating
- All changes have to be made through the app.
- If you don't sync often enough, it loses your data
- Sync can take a long time.
- The battery life is considerably shorter than I expected. It's about 2 1/2 days if I have constant sync turned off.
- Don't even bother with constant sync unless you're willing to take it off to charge a lot.
- All the music apps are paid

All in all, though, the pros are big and the cons are small. Enough that it still warrants a 5 star review.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Versa Smart Watch, Peach/Rose Gold Aluminium, One Size (S & L Bands Included), Heart Rate Monitor
